Laravel Boost guidelines for this Laravel application. Follow existing conventions and package versions: inertiajs/inertia-laravel v2, laravel/fortify v1, laravel/framework v12, laravel/prompts v0, laravel/wayfinder v0, laravel/boost v2, laravel/mcp v0, laravel/pail v1, laravel/pint v1, laravel/sail v1, pestphp/pest v4, phpunit/phpunit v12.

Skills: You MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain—don't wait until you're stuck.
- `wayfinder-development`: activate when referencing backend routes in frontend components, importing from `@/actions` or `@/routes`, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or working with Wayfinder route functions.
- `pest-testing`: activate when writing tests, creating unit or feature tests, adding assertions, testing Livewire components, browser testing, debugging test failures, working with datasets or mocking; or when the user mentions test, spec, TDD, expects, assertion, coverage, or needs to verify functionality works.

Follow application conventions; check sibling files for structure, approach, and naming. Use descriptive variable and method names. Check for existing components to reuse. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Unit and feature tests are more important. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise in explanations. If the user doesn't see a frontend change reflected in the UI, it could mean they need to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them.

Use Laravel Boost tools. Use the `list-artisan-commands` tool when you need to call an Artisan command to double-check the available parameters. Whenever you share a project URL with the user, you should use the `get-absolute-url` tool to ensure you're using the correct scheme, domain/IP, and port. You should use the `tinker` tool when you need to execute PHP to debug code or query Eloquent models directly. Use the `database-query` tool when you only need to read from the database. Use the `database-schema` tool to inspect table structure before writing migrations or models. You can read browser logs, errors, and exceptions using the `browser-logs` tool from Boost. Only recent browser logs will be useful - ignore old logs.

Search documentation before code changes. `search-docs` returns version-specific documentation; pass a package array to filter when useful. Use multiple broad, simple, topic-based queries. Do not add package names to queries. Query syntax: `authentication` uses auto-stemming; `rate limit` uses AND; `"infinite scroll"` is an exact phrase; `middleware "rate limit"` combines terms; `queries=["authentication", "middleware"]` matches ANY. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Inertia, Laravel, and Pest documentation and updated code examples.

Always use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`: `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods and functions; use appropriate PHP type hints for method parameters. Example: `protected function isAccessible(User $user, ?string $path = null): bool`. Typically, Enum keys are TitleCase. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex. Add useful array shape type definitions when appropriate.

The application runs on Laravel Herd at `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`; use `get-absolute-url` for valid URLs. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd.

Every change must be programmatically tested. Write a new test or update an existing test, then run the affected tests to make sure they pass. Run the minimum number of tests needed to ensure code quality and speed. Use `php artisan test --compact` with a specific filename or filter.

Inertia: Components live in `resources/js/pages` unless specified in `vite.config.js`. Use `Inertia::render()` for server-side routing instead of Blade views. Use v1/v2 features; check docs first. For deferred props, add an empty state with a pulsing or animated skeleton.

Laravel: Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (migrations, controllers, models, etc.); use `php artisan make:class` for generic PHP classes. You can list commands with `list-artisan-commands`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and the correct `--options`. Use Eloquent relationships with return type hints; prefer relationships and Eloquent models over raw queries/manual joins. Avoid `DB::`; prefer `Model::query()`. Use eager loading to prevent N+1 queries; use the query builder for very complex operations. For new models, create useful factories and seeders; ask whether the user needs anything else, using `list-artisan-commands` to check `php artisan make:model` options. For APIs, default to Eloquent API Resources and versioning unless existing routes do not, then follow convention. Always create Form Request classes for validation rather than inline controller validation; include rules and custom error messages. Check sibling Form Requests for array- or string-based rules. Use built-in authentication and authorization (gates, policies, Sanctum, etc.). Prefer named routes and `route()` for links. Use queued jobs for time-consuming operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files. Always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. For test models, use factories and check custom states first. Follow existing Faker conventions (`$this->faker` or `fake()`). Create tests with `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; use `--unit` for unit tests. Most tests should be feature tests. For `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest`, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Laravel 12 uses the streamlined Laravel 11 structure. Middleware are not registered in `app/Http/Kernel.php`; configure them declaratively in `bootstrap/app.php` using `Application::configure()->withMiddleware()`. Register middleware, exceptions, and routing files in `bootstrap/app.php`; providers in `bootstrap/providers.php`. `app\Console\Kernel.php` no longer exists; use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php`. Commands in `app/Console/Commands/` need no manual registration. When modifying a column, include all previously defined attributes in the migration or they will be dropped.
